title: Let Naam reach the sound of your speech
summary: The shabad joins saintly company, Naam, and inner peace until remembrance changes more than opinion. The mouth becomes gentler because the heart has stayed near the saints and kept the Beloved within.
takeaway: Let sangat and Naam shape the first sound you make.
lifeApplication: Before a tense exchange, remember the company you want forming you. Hold one Name inwardly, then let the first sentence prove that peace has reached the tongue.

source.shortMeaning: Saintly company and Naam bring peace that becomes audible in speech and visible in conduct.
source.lifeApplication: Let remembered sangat form your tone before pressure decides what your mouth will serve.

evidence.coreClaim: The cited lines show sweet speech as fruit from sangat and Naam, not as a performance of politeness.
evidence.turn: Speech is corrected at the heart's source before it is corrected at the tongue.
evidence.practicalImplication: Before a tense exchange, remember the company you want forming you. Hold one Name inwardly, then let the first sentence prove that peace has reached the tongue.
